exemplars.title: Criticmate: Stagewise Human-AI Co-Critique in Single-Screen UI Evaluation
exemplars.why: Criticmate makes a fixed Perception–Comprehension–Projection sequence its central interaction structure, gives each stage a distinct epistemic role, and preserves editability without letting users author the sequence.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above rid 4036 because its stages do more than organize task completion: they deliberately separate observation, interpretation, and action to prevent premature critique, making the pipeline more distinctive and conceptually transferable.

exemplars.title: Raising Awareness of Location Information Vulnerabilities in Social Media Photos using LLMs
exemplars.why: The interface exposes three fixed, functionally dependent phases—analysis, editing, and review—that take users from detecting privacy leaks through mitigation to verification.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above rid 10222 because the analysis–edit–review order has a stronger necessary dependency and closes a concrete safety loop, whereas CoAutoML's evidence chiefly establishes visible step-by-step progress.

exemplars.title: CoAutoML: User Interface Framework for Machine Learning Novices using LLM-based AutoML and Test-Driven Machine Teaching
exemplars.why: CoAutoML provides the clearest literal match to the structural signature: a visible workflow panel exposes five constant stages in order and displays the user's step-by-step progress through them.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above rid 10198 because its evidence explicitly establishes a user-visible ordered progress surface, while Athena's quote names three dependent phases but does not show how the interface exposes or governs advancement through them.

notes: The final selection follows the top three in the consensus order; no score was adjusted by more than 0.3. I slightly raised rid 4036 and rid 10222 because their evidence directly establishes visible phase structure or an ordered workflow panel. Readers should distrust any implied effectiveness claims: the supplied excerpts establish workflow design, not measured outcomes. Advancement enforcement is also not fully documented for any pick; Criticmate's evidence comes only from the abstract, rid 4036 from a figure caption, and CoAutoML's quote shows progress visibility but not explicit navigation constraints.
